thread.title: Sector ETF Week In Review For November 19-23

author: Hale Stewart
title: Sector ETF Week In Review For November 19-23
text:
Over the last few months, we've seen the sector rotation take a decidedly end-of-the-bull-run bent, with utilities, consumer staples and healthcare leading the pack. That trend continues:
While all sectors were down last week, the "best performers" were real estate, utilities, staples, and healthcare. Tech led the market lower thanks to a variety of factors: concerns about Apple's (NASDAQ: AAPL ) sales, the possibility of increased regulation for Facebook (NASDAQ: FB ), and trade war issues. Energy dropped thanks to oil's decline.
Once again, real estate is the leading industry for the last month, which is due to the Fed's tone becoming a bit more dovish. Basic materials are the number two performer; they outperformed thanks to positive trade talks. Staples is number three, utilities are number five, and healthcare is number six. Tech and energy are the worst performers - again.
For the last three months, defensive sectors are again leading the market with tech and energy the biggest losers.
Here's a chart showing the relative performance of all the major sectors:
Staples, utilities, and healthcare are leading SPY . Discretionary and tech - two sectors that outperform during the height of the bull market - are lagging the market. Basic materials and energy are moving to the improving section. Finally, notice that real estate is just on the other side of the leading quadrant.
Let's turn to the tech market sell-off to see what kind of damage this sector has experienced:
XLK broke its uptrend in early October. It fell to the 200-day EMA and traded around that level for about a month before continuing its move lower. The 10- and 20-day EMAs have moved below the 200-day EMA; the 50 is soon to follow. The 200-day EMA is moving modestly lower. Momentum is near year lows. The only good news on this chart is that volume has been decreasing, which indicates the sell-off might be nearing an end.
The 6-month charts of the 10 largest members aren't as hard as you might think. Apple comprises a little over 18% of the index; its price collapse over the last month and a half is a big contributor to XLK's drop. Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT ) is 17% of the ETF; its position isn't helping. Accenture (NYSE: ACN ), Cisco (NASDAQ: CSCO ), Oracle (NYSE: ORCL ), and Intel (NASDAQ: INTC ) are in fair shape; all are trading in the middle third of their respective charts. And it looks like IBM (NYSE: IBM ) may have bottomed.
Three of the ten largest members - Oracle, Cisco, and Accenture - are outperforming SPY. Intel is improving. Only two companies - Adobe (NASDAQ: ADBE ) and IBM - are lagging. Microsoft and Visa (NYSE: V ) are just barely weakening.
Does this mean that tech is a good contrarian play right now? I'm inclined to think not. The overall ETF performance referenced above has been in place for the last 4-6 months, indicating the market is becoming far more defensive. Tech's underperformance isn't technical; it's fundamental. And that makes this an unattractive sector - at least for now.
